title: Multivariate cohort matrix: continuous batching vs prefetch priming vs tiny-batch fallback
creator: Aisha Carter
description: Goal: Run a controlled multivariate experiment that compares three runtime strategies for token-level cost reduction while preserving latency SLOs and output quality: (A) continuous dynamic batching with adaptive batch size, (B) prefix/KV prefetch priming for repeated prefixes, and (C) tiny-batch fallback (low-latency single-request path) under tail conditions. This ticket defines the matrix, metric taxonomy, analysis plan, dashboards, and safe apply/rollback circuits for production canaries and cohort-based rollouts. The experiment prioritizes developer-facing production workloads (chat streaming and short-completion endpoints) and targets a measurable reduction in per-token cost without regressions in 95p latency, 99.9p error rate, and quality regressions measured by the prompt-eval harness.
success_criteria: 1) >=6% net unit-cost reduction for targeted cohorts with no more than 5% relative increase in 95p latency and no detectable quality regressions on the evaluation prompt set (alpha=0.05). 2) Automated safety gates trigger rollback if error_rate > 0.5% absolute or hallucination_score_degradation > 2% compared to baseline. 3) Clear decision matrix and dashboard artifacts for product/eng rollouts.
experiment_design: Matrix with 3 factors: batching strategy (continuous/adaptive vs static small batches), prefetch (on/off), and fallback threshold (latency-based tiny-batch fallback enabled/disabled). Cohorts: randomized by user_id hash into 10 equally sized cohorts to allow pairwise comparisons and pooled analysis. Canary ramp: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 25% traffic with safety gates evaluated at each step. Synthetic replay: use traffic-replay sandbox (ENG-28199) to validate economic model before canary.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis uses difference-in-differences across cohorts with bootstrap CIs and pre-registered A/B contrasts. For unit cost we control for request length and model variant. Quality regressions are tested against the canonical prompt-eval harness (PRD doc link below) with Benjamini-Hochberg correction for multiple comparisons. Generate per-cohort dashboards and an aggregated economics view. All analysis notebooks live in GH and will be exported to the experiment dashboard for review.
safety_and_rollbacks: Automated rollback circuits implemented in rollout-controller: if any of the hard gates fire (error_rate increase >0.5% absolute, 95p latency increase >100ms absolute, quality_eval_pval <0.01) the controller will automatically revert routing for affected cohorts and send an incident to #serve-ops. Soft gates (cost gains negative or ambiguous) pause ramp and require manual approval. A post-rollback forensic runbook and access checklist are included.
implementation_notes: Runtime changes required: add rollout-controller hook for multivariate traffic split, metrics tagging for cohort/treatment, and a light-weight prefetch predictor metric. Kernel selection unaffected; add tracing for KV cache prefetch latency. Instrument fallback path to record activation cause and observed latency. Feature flags are behind ff_serving_multivar and ff_prefetch_predictor.
